WV6-T01.4.note: Doubts 'kept from me' are hidden from the narrator, so 'concealed'; detaining, reserving, rearing and fulfilling do not apply to doubts withheld from someone.

exclusions.B: I still go back over that hour more often than I would like.
exclusions.C: The jar stood on Ilse's workshop shelf until she died; now it stands on mine, crack to the wall.
exclusions.D: That night I had watched it glow whiter than the rest and called out only the color of the fire.
exclusions.E: I still go back over that hour more often than I would like.

WV6-T01.5.note: The narrator keeps the jar crack-to-the-wall and dwells on having reported only the fire's color while the jar glowed whiter, implying regret over a missed warning; 'unease' is arguable from 'more often than I would like' but is less specific than regret.

WV6-T02.4.note: The object of 'settled' is the councillors themselves, who were satisfied and put at ease; 'resolved' is defensible only if read as settling their question rather than the people.

exclusions.A: The gate had at least ended the fires, but she hung her temperature loggers behind its solid panel, where any trapped warmth would gather first, and asked Brill to count the kilns as well, to see whether the bats had moved there.
exclusions.B: For years visitors forced their way in and lit fires inside the tunnel, so two autumns ago the county council fitted a steel gate to protect the bats: upright bars, with gaps wide enough for a bat but too narrow for a person, above a solid steel panel.
exclusions.C: Brill will be eighty in the spring, and he has begun teaching a neighbour's daughter to count.
exclusions.D: The loggers read a steady four degrees all winter, as cold as the tunnel had ever been, and the kilns, which visitors leave undisturbed, had suffered the same fall, losing two bats in every five.

WV6-T02.5.note: The gate stopped the fires and was cleared by the loggers and the kiln comparison, so keeping it is presented as sound; the author's unease in the last paragraph is about closing the file on the colony's future, not about the gate, though a reader could fold that into 'uneasy'.
